notes:
Buses: wires that carry 8, 16 or 32 bits, and the parts for them

A 32-bit CPU drawn with single wires would need hundreds of them per
connection. Pins now have a width, nets take theirs from the pins they
join (red where widths differ) and carry whole numbers. Switches,
constants and lamps get bits and a display format and become number
inputs and displays; gates and the multiplexer work bit by bit; new are
splitter and combiner, a register and a RAM. Buses are drawn thicker
with a slash and their width, their tooltip shows the value in decimal,
hex and signed, and formula tests read a wide switch or lamp as one
number. Own chips take the width of their switches and lamps.
